s1.syndrome_frame: asymptomatic cardiac abnormality with systolic murmur and abnormal ECG findings in a young adult
salient_findings: systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
key_facts: 29-year-old primigravida woman
no history of dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, or lower limb swelling
vital parameters within normal limits
systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
normal sinus rhythm with heart rate of 70 beats/min on ECG
complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
fragmented QRS with a notch on the R wave in inferior leads on ECG
no significant ST-T segment changes on ECG
dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on echocardiography
normal cardiac output on right-sided heart catheterization
step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium
pulmonary vascular resistance: 1.8 Wood units

raw.rationale: The presence of a large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt, dilated right atrium and right ventricle, and a step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium are consistent with an ostium secundum atrial septal defect, which is the most common type of atrial septal defect.

rejected.label: Ostium primum atrial septal defect
rejected.why: Typically associated with other congenital anomalies and often presents with more complex clinical features

rejected.label: Sinus venosus atrial septal defect
rejected.why: Usually associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection
rejected.why: Not directly supported by the echocardiography findings, which show a large defect with left-to-right shunt but do not specify anomalous pulmonary venous connection

rejected.label: Patent foramen ovale
rejected.why: Typically smaller and may not cause significant hemodynamic changes or dilatation of the right heart chambers
